dex.text: Rattles about on a loop of track, flattening hedges it was perfectly able to go round. It gets into ditches easily and out of them eventually.
dex.fact: The first tank, Little Willie, was built by William Foster and Co. of Lincoln in 1915. To keep the secret, the workers were told they were making water carriers for the desert, so people called them tanks, and the name stuck.

dex.text: A slab-sided iron giant that crosses trenches as if they were puddles. Inside it is hot, loud and full of fumes, and it seems to like it that way.
dex.fact: Tanks were first called landships, as the Royal Navy's Landships Committee ordered them. The rhomboid Mark I, with its tracks running right round the hull, first went into battle on the Somme in September 1916.
